items.prompt: What are the key components of an interactive calculator project with conditional logic?
items.title: Project: Interactive Calculator Architecture
items.content: The calculator should: 1) Accept user input for numbers and operation, 2) Use conditional logic (if/elif/else) to perform calculations, 3) Handle invalid inputs with error messages, 4) Display results. Plan the structure using functions for modularity (e.g., `get_input()`, `calculate()`, `display_result()`).

items.prompt: Design the architecture for an interactive calculator that supports addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. How will you structure the code to handle user input and perform operations based on user selection?
items.title: Project: Interactive Calculator Architecture
items.content: The calculator will use a while loop to continuously prompt users for input. A menu will display available operations (add, subtract, multiply, divide). User selection will determine which operation to perform. Input validation will ensure proper numerical entries. The code structure will separate operation logic into functions for clarity and reusability.

items.prompt: In the interactive calculator project, what code should be added to handle division by zero using conditional logic?
items.correct_answer: if divisor == 0: print('Error: Division by zero')
items.explanation: This conditional check prevents division by zero errors by validating the divisor before performing division, ensuring the program handles invalid inputs gracefully.
